item.text: I’ll query the workspace through the LixRay SQL API, then return each Markdown path with the exact matching line.

statements.sql:
WITH RECURSIVE
markdown_files(path, content) AS (
  SELECT path, replace(CAST(data AS TEXT), char(13), '')
  FROM lix_file
  WHERE (lower(path) LIKE '%.md' OR lower(path) LIKE '%.markdown')
    AND instr(CAST(data AS TEXT), 'TODO') > 0
),
lines(path, line_no, line, rest) AS (
  SELECT path,
         1,
         CASE WHEN instr(content, char(10)) > 0
              THEN substr(content, 1, instr(content, char(10)) - 1)
              ELSE content END,
         CASE WHEN instr(content, char(10)) > 0
              THEN substr(content, instr(content, char(10)) + 1)
              ELSE '' END
  FROM markdown_files
  UNION ALL
  SELECT path,
         line_no + 1,
         CASE WHEN instr(rest, char(10)) > 0
              THEN substr(rest, 1, instr(rest, char(10)) - 1)
              ELSE rest END,
         CASE WHEN instr(rest, char(10)) > 0
              THEN substr(rest, instr(rest, char(10)) + 1)
              ELSE '' END
  FROM lines
  WHERE rest <> ''
)
SELECT path, line_no, line
FROM lines
WHERE instr(line, 'TODO') > 0
ORDER BY path, line_no;

item.text: Lix SQL doesn’t support recursive CTEs for line splitting, so I’m using the API to select all matching Markdown blobs and extracting their matching lines exactly from those returned contents.

statements.sql:
SELECT path, CAST(data AS TEXT) AS content
FROM lix_file
WHERE (lower(path) LIKE '%.md' OR lower(path) LIKE '%.markdown')
  AND instr(CAST(data AS TEXT), 'TODO') > 0
ORDER BY path;
